1.why: All nine screens are static single-card layouts with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs; the only extra element is a static Logs panel.

2.why: Each page has one large bold heading and one high-contrast primary blue button, so the main action stands out, though the dark Logs panel competes visually for attention.

3.why: Each step presents a single field and a single action, making the next thing to do easy to locate, but the security codes/tokens must be hunted for in a technical Logs panel.

4.why: The flow requires remembering/transferring a 64-character token, two different six-digit codes, and a new 14+ character password across seven screens, with no visible progress indicator.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the sign-in and new-password steps.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no masked email, no remembered account, no saved device recognition; even the account contact field is empty and unlabelled with prior data.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain-language, and well spaced (e.g. 'Create a new password for your hospital account'), though jargon like 'recovery token' and 'multi-factor confirmation' remains.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the nine screenshots, so the claim that error messages explain the problem and the fix cannot be observed as true.

9.why: Step 1 shows 'Example: name@example.org or +15551234567', the password field states the 14–128 character rule, and code fields point to where the test code is found.

10.why: Each authentication step is clearly labelled (password, six-digit code), but no alternative methods such as face/biometric or passkey login are offered or explained.

11.why: Every screen offers only one primary action plus at most one secondary link, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Confirmation messages appear after key actions ('recovery instructions have been prepared', 'Privacy statement accepted'), though intermediate steps like password saved have no explicit success banner.

13.why: Short helper hints exist under most fields (token lifetime, code location, password rules), but there is no help link, tooltip, or 'what happens next' guidance for new steps.

14.why: No visible retry, 'resend code', 'start over', or back navigation is provided on any screen, so recovering from a mistake is not demonstrably easy.

15.why: All nine screens reuse the identical header, centered white card, heading style, blue primary button, helper text, and green safe-authentication notice.
